_comment: Per-machine config. config.json is gitignored. bootstrap.sh seeds config.json from this file only when config.json does not exist, and NOTHING writes config.json afterwards — only a human edits it. Pinned engine/tokenizer/GGUF/simplex-chat refs live in the committed pins.json, not here. Every machine keeps its own config.json. Top-level `timezone` is the IANA zone (e.g. America/Chicago) the agent reports local time in; empty means the host's local timezone.

navigation._comment: Navigation is two-stage at BOTH levels and the guards are the create doors (no threshold gate). Category: the softmax offers each existing category WITH its description (bare names carried no signal) plus create_category; confirm_category_fit then confirms the winner's scope (phase navigate:category_scope, P(covers) >= category_tau) and a rejected winner authors a new category. The `response` catchall and create_category share a boundary arbitrated by the actionability guard confirm_non_action (phase navigate:actionability, P(non_action) >= action_tau): the closed response tree is reached ONLY when the input is not a request, so a request no skill covers (e.g. "what is 255 * 12?") authors instead of getting a canned reply. Leaf: the softmax offers only existing skills; confirm_skill_fit then compares the winner's action to the request (phase navigate:intent, P(same) >= intent_tau) and a mismatch authors a new leaf. All three taus are separate from the top-level tau so tuning reuse-vs-create or actionability does not move run assessment/fidelity. The category check is deliberately permissive: with real descriptions in-scope requests score 0.9-1.0, so a borderline over-cover routes into a plausible category and the leaf guard catches it. A **category** softmax winner at or above `softmax_bypass_tau` (default 0.5) skips the scope confirm (traced `category_scope_bypassed`) — `create_category` is one of its options, so a confident winner really did beat authoring a category. The **leaf** intent guard is never bypassed: the leaf softmax offers only existing skills, so a confident winner is "best of the wrong lot", not a match, and the guard is the only leaf-level create door.

engine._comment: Per-machine engine settings only. The pinned engine/tokenizer/GGUF refs (semif_repo, semif_ref, gguf_url, gguf_sha256, source, revision) live in the committed pins.json — bumped on update, never per-machine config. The GGUF path is derived from pins.json's engine.gguf_url under .runtime/models/; set `gguf` here only to override it with a custom path.
engine._gpu_comment: gpu_layers: 0 keeps the CPU-only default, -1 offloads every layer, a positive count offloads that many. Requires a llama-cpp-python built with a GPU backend (bootstrap detects Vulkan/ROCm/CUDA). gpu_device picks the llama.cpp device index and gpu_split sets its split mode (0 = none).
engine._provider_comment: provider selects the decision engine, exactly like llm.provider/codegen.provider: "semif" (default) is the local llama.cpp GGUF described below; "winnow" is a remote /v1/systemone typed-decision API configured by the `winnow` block (a different model, e.g. Winnow-12B on a ROCm host). The engine is always real: a provider that cannot be reached raises EngineUnavailable, which is fatal — there is no fallback model. The decision log and `dream` cost work unchanged either way.

winnow._comment: Settings for provider == "winnow": a remote Winnow typed-decision server (`winnow-server`, ROCm/HIP on a dedicated GPU host) exposing POST /v1/systemone (choice questions) and /v1/chat/completions (text, used by llm.provider == "semif"). base_url is the server root; model is required (no default). timeout bounds each request; retries is the number of transient-failure retries before the engine is declared unavailable (0 = a single attempt; an unreachable engine is fatal by contract). api_key/api_key_env add a bearer token (usually unset on a LAN); extra_headers/user_agent pass through for custom setups. The Winnow model holds the whole GPU, so it cannot be resident alongside a large codegen model — stop one before starting the other.

llm._comment: Small OpenAI-compatible model that authors a new category/skill title + description (never the runnable body — that is `codegen` below). Deliberately its own endpoint/model, so it can be local and fast even when codegen is remote. Runs on THIS machine's local ollama; bootstrap reads base_url/model from here (a --llm-url/--llm-model flag overrides for that run only) and pulls `model` if it is missing. `model` is required (no default): set it to a model the endpoint serves. Uses the same provider machinery as codegen (real SSE stream, token budget, idle watchdog); short JSON replies. Sampler params (temperature/top_p/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty) are opt-in: an unset value is omitted from the request so the server's model default applies — set them here only when you know the right values for the model. The draft is authored asynchronously by a single-slot worker and the request re-runs when it lands; an unreachable endpoint is graceful (traced, user notified), not fatal. disable_thinking sends reasoning_effort:none so a reasoning model answers the short JSON directly instead of spending the reply budget on hidden chain-of-thought (set false only for an endpoint that rejects the parameter). provider selects the transport: "ollama" (default; a local OpenAI-compatible server, context auto-detected via /api/show), "opencode" (the hosted OpenCode Console inference API at https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1 — set model to a Chat Completions family id such as kimi-k2.7-code or glm-5.3, and provide api_key or api_key_env; the ollama probe is skipped), or "semif" (the loaded SemIf decision GGUF generates in-process via SemIfEngine.generate — no endpoint/model/api_key is used; see the `semif` block below).

semif._comment: Settings for provider == "semif": the already-loaded SemIf engine model generates the text in-process (the same GGUF the decision engine scored with), so no base_url/model/api_key is used and `model` above is not required. temperature 0 = greedy decoding; max_tokens bounds the reply length (callers may override per call). Generation shares the engine's lock with decision scoring, so a reply briefly serializes against routing/assessment.

codegen._comment: OpenAI-compatible model that writes runnable skill bodies. Runs on a REMOTE ollama host (bootstrap reads base_url/model from here; a --codegen-url/--codegen-model flag overrides for that run only); the local small model is `llm` above. `model` is required (no default): set it to a code-capable model the endpoint serves. Bodies perform real actions against the user's configured services via stdlib transports, read every operational value from ctx.config, and declare their integration (INTEGRATION: service/transport/config_vars). Larger/slower than the decision or title/description model. The transport always streams so the client-side token budget (output cap / peak total fill) can abort a runaway in real time; stream only toggles console echo of tokens. timeout is total seconds; idle_warn/idle_timeout surface a silent (wedged) stream. The context window is auto-detected via ollama /api/show; context_window is the manual fallback (0 = auto/default 100000). smart_limit/warn_limit and max_fill_ratio/warn_fill_ratio bound total fill; max_output caps streamed output (>=1 absolute tokens, 0<x<1 fraction of window); chars_per_token converts chars to the token estimate. temperature/top_p/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty are opt-in: an unset value is omitted from the request so the server's model/Modelfile default applies; set them here only when you know the right values for the model. A rejected body retries with a fresh short prompt (max_attempts attempts), reusing the same sampler params. elicitation asks the product owner implementation questions before the body is written (posted to the question queue; every front end defers). After the body lands it is reviewed for real-action fidelity, then the data contract (contract.json) is derived in a separate call, then skill.test.py (hermetic mechanics test: loopback http.server for HTTP bodies, fixtures inline, no external network) in a shared-context call, and the test is auto-run as a subprocess (test_timeout seconds); on failure a 3-option SemIf decision (code/contract/test) regenerates the failing piece, bounded by test_max_attempts. contract_search.enabled auto-populates the skill config.json via SemIf against the global + category config. provider selects the transport: "ollama" (default; local OpenAI-compatible server, context auto-detected via /api/show) or "opencode" (the hosted OpenCode Console inference API at https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1 — set model to a Chat Completions family id such as kimi-k2.7-code, glm-5.3, or deepseek-v4.1-flash, and provide api_key or api_key_env; the ollama probe is skipped).

elicitation._comment: Ask the product owner implementation questions before the body is written: which service/account, how to connect, where the credential comes from, what success looks like. Every front end defers questions to the questions panel; the single-slot writer asks them one at a time and waits answer_timeout seconds for each (the clock resets on every answer submit, so the user only ever sees the next question after answering the current one; a timeout stops the sequence). wait_timeout is the separate, longer wait for the optional creation-approval gate. Questions never ask for operational data values (collected at first fire) or config-vs-input cadence (the config step owns that).

fidelity._comment: After the body lands, an authoring:fidelity SemIf decision (accept/reconsider, P(reconsider) >= tau or any static finding) checks whether it really performs the action vs simulates it (canned result, fabricated data, draft-by-default). Static INTEGRATION checks (declaration vs code) run alongside. The gate never diagnoses: a rejected body is regenerated with the raw evidence bundle, bounded by max_attempts; a still-fake body is accepted but traced/badged, never a hard authoring failure.

repair._comment: A failed real run triggers a logged SemIf repair choice (retry / repair_skill / ask_user / no_repair) surfaced in the REPL and dashboard. Executing a repair is user-confirmed (a codegen write is slow); body repairs are bounded by max_attempts per skill and carry the observed failure into the regeneration.

contract_search._comment: After the data contract lands, run a SemIf choice per variable to auto-populate the skill config.json from the global config and the category config (data/skills/<category>/config.json). Logged as phase config:search.

degeneration._comment: SemIf degeneration watchdog: while the body streams, a 2-option SemIf decision (continue/stop) is made every `interval` chars against the last `window` chars of content+reasoning (once `min_chars` have accumulated); P(stop) >= threshold aborts the write with a graceful stub. Recorded trace-only (kind `codegen`), never in the decision log. Disabled when no engine is available.

simplex_chat._comment: Per-machine simplex-chat daemon settings. The pinned binary (version/bin_url/sha256) lives in the committed pins.json, not here. The command gateway talks to the daemon on `port` (profile .runtime/simplex/, unit semif-simplex.service). The SimpleX forwarding bridge owns its OWN daemon/profile on `forward_port` (profile .runtime/simplex-forward/, unit semif-simplex-forward.service) so messaging UX never shares the command bot's identity. bootstrap.sh renders both units from these values. gateway.simplex.ws_url must match `port`; bridges.simplex.ws_url must match `forward_port`.

bridges._comment: Standalone third-party API bridges: a simple, secure local HTTP layer between codegen-authored skill bodies and real system services. Each bridge runs as its own process (`python -m semif_agent.cli bridge [--name NAME]`), one process per service daemon, and never runs inside the command gateway — gateway isolation is non-negotiable (see AGENTS.md). The bridge catalog (names, endpoints, config vars) is injected into the code-generation prompts via `semif_agent.bridges.describe_bridges()`.

simplex._comment: SimpleX forwarding bridge: buffers every inbound DM (no allowlist — the point is to see who reached the bot through its invite link), and serves invite-link / read / send over HTTP. It owns its own simplex-chat daemon/profile (`ws_url`, `forward_port` above), separate from the command gateway's. Skills call it at http://host:port (derived from this block; no top-level duplicate). Binds localhost only; an optional `token` is required in the X-Semif-Token header when set.

llm._comment: LLM bridge: a generic `POST /chat` in front of the agent's configured `llm` model, so skill bodies can ask for short generated text (e.g. an event title + description) over HTTP instead of speaking the OpenAI-compatible protocol. It reuses the top-level `llm` client (endpoint/model/sampler configured once there); this block only carries the local listener. Skills call it at http://host:port (derived from this block; no top-level duplicate). Binds localhost only; an optional `token` is required in the X-Semif-Token header when set. It runs inside the same `semif-bridge.service` process as the other enabled bridges.

nextcloud._comment: Nextcloud bridge: files (WebDAV), calendar events and tasks (CalDAV), contacts (CardDAV), and Notes (the Notes app) over one uniform local JSON API, so skill bodies never speak the native DAV/OCS protocols. It has no service daemon (Nextcloud is plain HTTPS) and runs inside the same `semif-bridge` process as the other enabled bridges. The connection is configured HERE (url/username/app_password); when a value is blank the bridge falls back to the top-level nextcloud_url/nextcloud_username/nextcloud_app_password/nextcloud_default_calendar the calendar seeds already use, so the account is configured once. `app_password` is a Nextcloud app password (Settings > Security > Devices & sessions), not the account password. `default_calendar`/`default_addressbook` are used when a request names none and the account has several. `verify_tls` false skips certificate verification (self-signed hosts). Skills call it at http://host:port (derived from this block; no top-level duplicate). Binds localhost only; an optional `token` is required in the X-Semif-Token header when set.

gateway._comment: Messenger COMMAND intake — and nothing else. `python -m semif_agent.cli gateway` runs one or more platforms (`--platform simplex,lxmf` or `all`) in a SINGLE process sharing one scheduler/skill store — never run two gateway processes over one store. Each platform feeds authorized DM text through the normal gate/score/queue/dispatch pipeline; results, authoring questions, and repair offers are sent back to the originating chat. It must never read a contact's history, show/create invite links, or compose on the user's behalf — that is the independent bridge services' job (`bridges`). home_channel receives messages whose origin chat is unknown (e.g. a background repair offer). reply_prefix is prepended to every reply. text_batch_delay concatenates rapid-fire messages from one contact.

humanize._comment: Optional LLM cleanup of a skill's result line for chat replies. Off by default. When enabled, a completed result is unwrapped from the scheduler's `<skill>: <ok|failed> — <detail>` bookkeeping and rewritten by the scheduler's `llm` client into one grounded, friendly sentence; it never decides success/failure and always falls back to the raw result on any error. `timeout`/`max_tokens`/`max_chars` bound the auxiliary call (a slow cleanup must not hold the gateway). A platform turns it on/off with its own `humanize` key (bool or `{enabled: ...}`), overriding this global default; `timeout`/`max_tokens`/`max_chars` are global. Only result lines are cleaned — questions, repair/approval notices, and status chatter are untouched.

simplex._comment: SimpleX command adapter. Connects to the command simplex-chat daemon (`simplex_chat.port`) over its JSON WebSocket API. Requires the optional `websockets` package (lazy-imported; the gateway refuses to start without it). allowed_users entries match either a numeric contactId or a display name; default is deny-all unless allow_all_users is set. Groups/attachments are not supported.

lxmf._comment: LXMF (Reticulum) command adapter. Runs IN-PROCESS — there is no external daemon; `pip install lxmf` provides the transport (optional, lazy-imported; the gateway refuses to start with an install hint). The bot's reachable address is its LXMF delivery destination hash (32 hex chars), printed on connect. config_dir/storage_path hold Reticulum's config and the persisted identity under .runtime/lxmf/ so the address is stable across restarts (empty = the .runtime/lxmf defaults). allowed_users entries match the peer's LXMF address (32 hex chars) or a best-effort display name; default is deny-all unless allow_all_users is set. desired_method is 'direct' (reliable link) or 'opportunistic' (single packet). propagation_node is an optional LXMF propagation-node address (hex) for store-and-forward.

voice._comment: Voice command adapter: a local microphone front end with wake word + speech-to-text + text-to-speech. Requires the optional voice stack (requirements/voice.txt; sounddevice + openwakeword + faster-whisper + piper-tts + onnxruntime; the system needs libportaudio2). Lazy-imported; the gateway refuses to start with an install hint. Runs best in the user's audio session (foreground `gateway --platform voice`), not a headless systemd user service. Audio is 16 kHz mono int16; capture/playback run at the device's native rate and are resampled to/from 16 kHz (capture_sample_rate/output_sample_rate override it; 0 = the device default). wake.model is an openWakeWord model name or path (bootstrap downloads models into the venv, where they resolve by name; model_dir is an optional local dir for a custom model file); stt.model is a faster-whisper size/path (cached under .runtime/hf); tts.voice is a Piper voice id or path (bootstrap downloads it under .runtime/voice/tts). After each reply the next utterance is accepted without the wake word for follow_up_window_s. result_only speaks just the skill's result line (dropping queue/urgency bookkeeping and the `<skill>: ok —` wrapper) instead of the full scheduler output; set false for the complete text. max_speak_chars truncates long replies before speaking. chat_id identifies the single local session; home_channel defaults to it so timers/repair offers are spoken too.

cue._comment: Audible feedback. A short sine beep plays when the wake word fires so you know you're being heard; set submit_frequency > 0 for a second beep once the utterance is transcribed. volume is 0..1.
